text.150_Siman, 0_Comment, 0_Paragraph: "You are near in their mouths but far from their innermost being"—this is difficult to understand: why does the verse not use consistent language, saying either "in their mouths" and "in their innermost being" or both differently? The answer given is:
text.150_Siman, 0_Comment, 1_Paragraph: This refers to people who express sin outwardly—for example, through mocking, blasphemy, or obscene speech—yet they say that God will forgive them. They claim, "The Rock (God) will pardon us." Thus, the verse states: "You are near in their mouths," meaning they verbally declare that God is close and will forgive them for the evil they say. However, in truth, "You are far from their innermost being," meaning from their true thoughts—because deep down, they believe that God will not actually forgive them, as they are aware of the severity of their wrongdoing.
